newsitem.title: THAILAND: Lame-duck Thai premier to attend APEC summit.
newsitem.headline: Lame-duck Thai premier to attend APEC summit.

text.p: Thailand's lame-duck prime minister Banharn Silpa-archa will attend the upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum in the Philippines, a government spokesman said on Tuesday.
Banharn's Chart Thai Party, which lost substantial support in Sunday's general election, has been excluded from a coalition formed after the elections due to its scandal-tainted image.
Banharn will sit on the opposition benches after the new government takes office -- probably in early December.
He will depart for Manila on November 24, then on to Subic Bay the next day for the summit meeting of the leaders of the 18 APEC member-countries.
His attendance is expected to be mostly ceremonial. He is not likely to make any policy statements and has no bilateral discussions planned with other leaders, the spokesman said.

The New Aspiration Party (NAP) led by Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh won the election with a slim two-seat victory over its rival, the Democrat Party. Chavalit has been nominated for the premiership by his five coalition members.
Banharn's Chart Thai Party, weakened by the defections of many senior politicians to the NAP, came fourth in the poll.
